about: Authored understanding of a player's own words in the dialogue window (Docs/Design/84 §13.5, Phase 13): what the window answers typed words with when the NPC Mind isn't connected, or a call to it fails. The words are normalised (lower case, contractions spelt out, punctuation gone, the resident's own name and filler left out), the world's slots are found (a resident by name, a place by name or kind, an issue, a kin word, a good, the wearer's quirk, the player's own name), and each intent is scored by its cues: a cue is a run of words that must appear in that order, with a weight; `whole` cues must be all that was said; `slot` cues count only when that slot was found; `needs` refuses an intent without its slot; `start` cues must open what was said; an intent's `not` words cost it 0.4 (work asked for a Chapter is a mission); a `minor` intent (a greeting, thanks, yes, no...) loses 0.3 beside a question scoring 0.55 or more ("Hello, I'm Bramble" is the introduction). Filler is left out at the start, the ways of addressing someone at either end; `quirk_words` widen a quirk's own words. The best intent's confidence is its score less a share of the next best's; under `threshold` the resident says it didn't follow (dlg.<tree>.unclear). Core/RatwUnderstand.cpp reads it; Tests/fixtures/understand_corpus.jsonl (500 player lines) gates it in ctest (W2).
